DATED:
 
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (QUASHING) NO. 10499 of 2025  With  R/SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION NO. 10101 of 2023  ==========================================================
 DARSHAN JITENDRABHAI GAJJAR (SUTHAR)
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR HB CHAMPAVAT(6149) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR HARDIK MEHTA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HASMUKH D. SUTHAR  Date : 05/08/2025  COMMON ORAL ORDER Registry to accept vakalatnama of learned advocate Mr. Rutvij Oza, who has instructions to appear for respondent No.2 in Special Criminal Application No.10499/2025.
[1.0] RULE.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned advocates waive service of note of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.

[2.0] Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and since it is jointly stated at the Bar by learned advocates on both the sides that the dispute between the parties has been resolved amicably,
this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

[3.0] By way of these petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as "BNSS"), the petitioners i.e. husband and in-laws of respondent No.2 have prayed to quash and set aside the FIR being CR NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/10499/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/08/2025 undefined No.11216001230447 of 2023 registered with Adalaj Police Station, District Gandhinagar for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 Darshan Jitendrabhai Gajjar (Suthar) vs State Of Gujarat on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179796776/
1 and sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and to quash all other consequential proceedings arising therefrom filed at the instance of respondent No.2 - original complainant.
[4.0] Learned advocates for the respective parties submitted that during the pendency of proceedings, the parties have settled the dispute amicably and pursuant to such mutual settlement,
respondent No.2 has also filed an Affidavit dated 01.08.2025 which is taken on record.

In the Affidavit, the original complainant has categorically stated that the dispute with the petitioners has been resolved amicably and that she has no objection, if the present proceedings are quashed and set aside since there is no surviving grievance between them.
[5.0] It is necessary to consider whether the power conferred by the High Court under section 482 of the CrPC is warranted.
It is true that the powers under Section 482 of the Code are very wide and the very plenitude of the power requires great caution in its exercise.
The Court must be careful to see that its decision in exercise of this power is based on sound principles.
The inherent power should not be exercised to stifle a legitimate prosecution.

The High Court being the highest court of a State should normally refrain from giving a prima facie decision in a case where the entire facts are incomplete and hazy, more so when the evidence has not been collected and produced before NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/10499/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/08/2025 undefined the Court and the issues involved, whether factual or legal, are of magnitude and cannot be seen in their true perspective without sufficient material.

Of course, no hard-and-fast rule can be laid down in regard to cases in which the High Court will exercise its extraordinary jurisdiction of quashing the proceeding at any stage as the Hon'ble Supreme Court has decided in the case of Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Ravi Shankar Srivastava, IAS & Anr., reported in AIR 2006 SC 2872.

entities.text: Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Ravi Shankar Srivastava, IAS & Anr., reported in AIR 2006 SC 2872
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[6.0] Having heard learned advocates on both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case as also the principle laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of (i) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303,
(ii) Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, (iii) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, (iv) Manoj Sharma Vs.
State & Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and (v) Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr.
reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC) as also considering the fact that settlement is arrived at between the parties and even, the complainant has remained personally present in the Court and affirmed the factum of her filing the affidavit, in the opinion of this Court, the further continuation of criminal proceedings against the present petitioners in relation to the impugned FIR would cause unnecessary harassment to the petitioners.

sentences.text: Further, the continuance of trial pursuant to the mutual settlement arrived at between the parties would be a futile exercise.

Hence, to secure the ends of justice, it would be appropriate to quash NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/10499/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/08/2025 undefined and set aside the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof under Section 528 of the BNSS.
[7.0] In the result, petitions are allowed.
The impugned FIR being CR No.11216001230447 of 2023 registered with Adalaj Police Station, District Gandhinagar as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof
are hereby quashed and set aside qua the petitioners herein.
